sentences.text: Fully grown Plateosaurus individuals ranged from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and weighed between 600 and 4000 kilograms.
The skull of Plateosaurus was small, narrow, and rectangular in side view, nearly three times as long as it was high.
Plateosaurus had proportionally long lower legs and metatarsi, indicating it could run quickly on its hind limbs.
Features of its teeth and jaw suggest Plateosaurus fed primarily or exclusively on plants.
Johann Friedrich Engelhardt discovered vertebrae and leg bones of Plateosaurus at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany, in 1834.
The genus Plateosaurus was described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
Excavations in a clay pit in Saxony-Anhalt between the 1910s and 1930s revealed between 39 and 50 Plateosaurus skeletons.
More than 100 skeletons of Plateosaurus have been found.
Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivore.
The lack of forelimb pronation meant Plateosaurus was an obligate biped, unable to walk in any other way.
Plateosaurus commonly lived for at least 12 to 20 years.
No fossil of Plateosaurus has yet been discovered containing gastroliths (gizzard stones) in the stomach area.
Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, often referred to as a prosauropod.
The type species of Plateosaurus is Plateosaurus trossingensis.
As of 2019, only three species of Plateosaurus are universally accepted as valid: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic epoch, approximately 214 to 204 million years ago.
Plateosaurus lived in what is now Central and Northern Europe.
P. gracilis is found in the Löwenstein Formation (lower to middle Norian), while P. trossingensis and P. longiceps come from the Trossingen Formation (upper Norian).
It is debated whether much prosauropod material from the German Knollenmergel labeled as Plateosaurus actually belongs to the type species or to Plateosaurus at all.
Some researchers debate whether plateosaurs were the direct ancestors of sauropods.
Paul Barrett hypothesized that Plateosaurus may have been an omnivore, supplementing its herbivorous diet with small prey or carrion.
There is no extended consensus on the taxonomy of Plateosaurus species, as other species have been assigned in the past.
